title: Closed specializations in finite-type stacks with quasi-compact diagonal
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $\mathcal X$ be an algebraic stack of finite type over $k$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]: it is quasi-compact and its structural morphism is locally of finite type on smooth scheme charts. Suppose the diagonal of $\mathcal X$ is quasi-compact and separated, with quasi-compactness interpreted by [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Give $|\mathcal X|$ the field-point set and smooth-atlas topology of [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology]. This topological space is Noetherian and sober: descending chains of closed subsets stabilize, and every nonempty irreducible closed subset has a unique generic point. In particular every nonempty closed subset of $|\mathcal X|$ contains a point whose singleton is closed in $|\mathcal X|$. The empty stack is allowed. No quasi-finiteness of the diagonal is assumed.

source.place: Tags 06R6 (lemma-locally-finite-type-locally-noetherian), 0DQI (lemma-Noetherian-topology), and 0DQQ (lemma-sober-qs). Last clause follows by choosing a minimal nonempty closed subset in a Noetherian T0 space. This is the closed-point selection used in Alper Lemma 8.3.1, printed p.39.

proof.text: By [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism], choose a smooth surjective atlas $p:U\to\mathcal X$ with $U$ a quasi-compact scheme. The finite-type hypothesis, tested on smooth charts, says $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type. Every ideal of a field is zero or the unit ideal, hence finitely generated [def-weil-field, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; thus $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian by [def-weil-affine-spectrum, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to this scheme morphism to see that $U$ is locally Noetherian. Together with its quasi-compactness this makes $U$ a Noetherian scheme.

By [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology], $|p|$ is surjective and inverse images of closed subsets of $|\mathcal X|$ are closed in $|U|$. Given a nonempty family $\mathcal F$ of closed subsets of $|\mathcal X|$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] to the family $\{|p|^{-1}(F):F\in\mathcal F\}$. Choose $F_0$ whose inverse image is minimal. A strict inclusion $F\subsetneq F_0$ would give a strict inclusion of inverse images, by surjectivity, a contradiction. Hence every such family has a minimal member; in particular any descending chain of closed subsets stabilizes at its minimal member. This proves Noetherianity, and also provides the minimal-member form needed below.

The assumed quasi-compactness of $\mathcal X$ and its diagonal together with the affine base $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-qc-stack-spectral-point-space]. Consequently $|\mathcal X|$ is spectral, and thus sober by the definition [def-weil-spectral-space]. The separatedness assumption on the diagonal is allowed but unnecessary in this application.

Let $C$ be nonempty and closed. Step 2 gives a minimal nonempty closed subset $D\subseteq C$. For each $y\in D$, the closure $\overline{\{y\}}$ is nonempty, closed and contained in $D$, so equals $D$. This closure is irreducible: if contained in a union of two closed subsets, $y$ lies in one, and then its whole closure lies there. Thus every point of $D$ is a generic point of the same nonempty irreducible closed subset $D$. Sobriety from step 3 forces all these points to coincide. Hence $D=\{y\}$ is closed in $|\mathcal X|$, proving the claimed closed-point existence. For the empty stack there is no nonempty $C$, so this last assertion is vacuous.

All four steps are correct, and the statement, stmt_deps and source are unchanged. (1) The quasi-compact atlas from def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism is locally of finite type over Spec k. k is Noetherian, so pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft gives a Noetherian scheme U. (2) lem-sfb-stack-point-topology gives a surjective |p| and the closed-preimage criterion. With the minimal-closed-family leaf, surjectivity carries strict inclusions down to the preimages, which gives the minimal-member form and DCC. (3) The new node with S=Spec k gives sobriety. (4) A minimal nonempty closed D ⊆ C has every point generic, sobriety forces D={y}, and the point is closed in all of |X|. New node lem-sfb-qc-stack-spectral-point-space: it is Stacks 0DQN specialised to an affine base, which is true because Δ_{X/S} is qc iff the absolute diagonal is (base change of the closed immersion S→S×S). I tested it on the empty stack, Spec of a non-Noetherian ring, BG and an affine variety. It is statement-only and self-contained, with no Noetherian overclaim. It supplies only the sobriety input in a wider setting, not a restatement of the item: steps 1-2 and 4 carry the Noetherian and closed-point work. A grep -R over the DAG for the tags/labels and for spectral/sober together with stack finds no duplicate. Batch-5 check: the new citations (def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism, lem-sfb-stack-point-topology) reach only the general definition def-trf-algebraic-space, which is not part of the trace-formula or Poincaré duality proofs, and the item already cites all three on the base. No SGA citation. Blueprint ancestor None is inherited and consistent. No tool_uses needed.

lean.statement: theorem finite_type_stack_closed_specialization (k : Type u) [Field k] (F : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (hF : IsAlgebraicModuliStack F) (hqc : IsQuasiCompactModuli F) (hft : ∀ (U : Over (Spec (.of k))) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)) F), IsSmoothModuliAtlas F U a → LocallyOfFiniteType U.hom) (hdiag : ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (t : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T)) (moduliTwoFiberProduct (moduliBaseStructure F) (moduliBaseStructure F))), ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of k))) (p : Z.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T), HasSpaceBaseChange (moduliRelativeDiagonal (moduliBaseStructure F)) T t Z p ∧ AlgebraicSpace.MapIsQuasiCompact p ∧ AlgebraicSpace.MapToSchemeIsSeparated Z T p) : TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace (ModuliPoints F) ∧ (∀ C : Set (ModuliPoints F), IsClosed C → IsIrreducible C → ∃! x : ModuliPoints F, IsGenericPoint x C) ∧ (∀ C : Set (ModuliPoints F), IsClosed C → C.Nonempty → ∃ x ∈ C, IsClosed ({x} : Set (ModuliPoints F)))
